author: Marilyn Upchurch
title: Protestors voice ICE facility contract concerns at New Mexico Roundhouse - NewsBreak
text:
By Marilyn Upchurch ,
5 hours ago
SANTA FE, N.M. (KRQE) – Protesters gathered outside the Roundhouse Wednesday, pressing state leaders to do something about what they call bad conditions inside United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement facilities.
Story continues below
Protesters said counties and detention facilities need to stop entering contracts with ICE to detain immigrants. They hoped state lawmakers would address that during the special session. “When we first saw that the governor was thinking of having some kind of an ICE detention on the agenda, we thought that it was because everything that’s happening nationally. To see it just not be on the agenda and pushed to January, the urgency is there, so it should also be reflected in New Mexico’s politics,” said one protestor who wanted to remain anonymous.
During their demonstrations, protesters posed inside make-shift cells as they read testimonies of individuals inside ICE facilities in New Mexico, describing deplorable conditions. This comes after Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham and Democrats originally raised the possibility of addressing immigration detention facilities at the special session, but it was not added to the agenda.
In the past, Democrats have said they want to ban state and local governments from contracting with ICE, but protestors said action needs to be taken now. “New Mexico is very well positioned to join many other states and ending our complicity in the private prison carceral system for the detention of immigrants. New Mexico has an opportunity to end our complicity in that to instead invest in the infrastructure and education that brings up all members of our community,” said Jovanny Hernandez, a protestor on Wednesday.
Back in August, a group of Republicans and one Democrat toured the Otero County Processing Center , which houses ICE detainees. At the time, the Republicans told KRQE News 13 that they didn’t see any problems inside, and they endorsed the facility’s continued operation for the jobs that it creates, as well as its role in fighting crime.
The protesters cleared out in the afternoon. They hope this issue will be brought up in the 30-day legislative session coming up in January.
There are three ICE detention facilities in New Mexico. Those facilities are in Otero, Torrance, and Cibola counties.
